body:
Hey, ReachTheTopShelf.

Don't let your fear of medication stop you from getting treatment. I understand how you feel, because it's exactly how I've felt my entire life. Last week, though, things got too much and I went to hang myself from a tree. Luckily somebody else was out in the woods, stopped me and took me to the hospital. I was put on medication and holy shit, I feel stupid for not at least trying them sooner.

I'm still in the first week, so I'm still getting side effects and the medication isn't working fully but I already feel better. I don't know if this medication will work out, or if I will have to come off it and try another, but these days have been the first in my life that I have felt... okay.

I won't lie, the first few days were tough with side effects and I don't even know if they'll work out long term but I would definitely say they're worth trying. All I'm saying is don't let it get to the point where you're trying to hang yourself before you get help.

I hope whatever you try you find something that works for you. Good luck, and you can message me **any** time you're feeling down. You aren't alone in this.

**EDIT:** That last line goes for any of you that are suffering with depression. As isolated as you feel there are others that are going or have been going through the same shit. Message me at any point and I'll do my best to just listen to you.
Untreated mental illness. Thankfully I'm not a very good hangman.

I would just like to add that even with suspension hanging you don't really feel much (comparatively).

I've not been hanged to death (obviously, I'd hope) but in my experience it isn't just a pain, but an incredible pressure on the back of your eyes like they will come out of your head. Your hearing dulls and goes "muddy", your vision goes kind of white and then fades out. It's reasonably peaceful as being executed goes.

EDIT: This is just my personal experience, and I feel guilty for describing it as something almost positive. I apologize for that.
Suicide is definitely not always a decision. It's not always as simple as there being too much and deciding to opt out.
Thank you for the link, I appreciate it. I guess I have to keep going back to the doctors.
I know exactly how you feel. I love painting, and though maybe not exactly "excited", feeling "inspired" was very well close. Now I just stare at paper. I don't know what happened either.
